sections.content:
Now I understand the mechanic better. The RIGHT action extends a horizontal path to the right. The path consists of alternating white (w) 2x3 blocks and gray (g) single pixels as separators. 
Before RIGHT: path ended at column 22 (last w block at 38,20-39,22)
After RIGHT: path extended with new segments at columns 23-25 and 26-28
The colored blocks are at columns 42-45. The path needs to reach there. Currently the path ends at column 28, so I need about (42-28)/3 ≈ 5 more RIGHT moves to reach the red block.
But wait - the efficiency budget says ~61 target actions and I've used 1. That's a LOT of actions. Maybe the path extends slowly, one tile at a time? Let me check: each RIGHT added 2 new w blocks (6 cells each = 12 cells total changed). The path seems to extend by about 6 columns per RIGHT action (from col 22 to col 28).
Actually, looking more carefully:
- Before: last w block at (38,20)-(39,22), ending at col 22
- After: new w blocks at (38,23)-(39,25) and (38,26)-(39,28), ending at col 28
So each RIGHT extends the path by 6 columns (two 3-wide segments). The colored blocks start at col 42. From col 28, I need (42-28)/6 ≈ 2.3, so about 3 more RIGHT moves.
But 61 target actions seems like a lot for just extending a path. Maybe I need to extend to each of the 3 colored blocks separately? Or maybe the path needs to go all the way and then something else happens?
Let me try extending more to see what happens when the path reaches a colored block. I'll batch several RIGHT moves.

# Extend path toward the colored blocks - try 3 RIGHT moves
result = action(['RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT'])

# Check path extent after

for n in seg:
    if n['color'] == 'w' and n['pixels'] == 4:
        b = n['boundary']
        max_c = max(p[1] for p in b)

        if min_r < 50:
            path_nodes.append(max_c)
print(f"Path w-block right edges: {sorted(path_nodes)}")
print(f"Path extends to column: {max(path_nodes) if path_nodes else 'N/A'}")

# Check if any colored blocks changed
for n in seg:
    if n['color'] in ('R', 'b', 'N') and n['pixels'] == 16:
        b = n['boundary']
        min_r = min(p[0] for p in b)
        if min_r < 50:
            print(f"Colored block: color={n['color']}, bbox rows {min(p[0] for p in b)}-{max(p[0] for p in b)}, cols {min(p[1] for p in b)}-{max(p[1] for p in b)}")
</parameter>
</function>
